text:
sam: heads up — I found a reproducible silent-corruption when activation quant is enabled (FP8) and we pick the new packed matmul kernel. no crash, but outputs diverge from FP16 baseline consistently for long sequences.
anya: can you paste the repro steps? does it require KV cache? :eyes:
sam: yes KV cache + continuous batching seems necessary. short seqs don't show it. repro command below.
```bash
# repro (dev machine, cuda12)
python -m redwood.tests.repro_fp8 \
  --model models/llama-small \
  --seq 1536 \
  --batch 4 \
  --kv-cache \
  --use-fp8-activation
```
kevin: does it only happen with matmul_fp8_pack_v2 or with any FP8 kernel?
sam: reproduced only when we pick matmul_fp8_pack_v2. forcing fp16 kernel restores correct outputs.
jen: can you dump the kernel selection / perf log snippet?
sam: pasted below. note the scale mismatch warning is subtle and was previously filtered out.
```
[perf] selected_kernel=matmul_fp8_pack_v2 seq=1536 batch=4 latency=12.3ms
[debug] activation_scale=0.125 quant_clip=127 scales=(0.125,0.124)
[warn] per-column-scale-diff > 0.008 -> continuing (was previously an assert)
[debug] kv_cache_offset=8192 kv_cache_preserve=True
[assert] output_hash=0x9a3f -> expected 0x9a2c
```
kevin: interesting — per-column scaling drift + reusing KV cache buffers could lead to a misaligned scale being applied during accumulation. that would be silent.
anya: do we have a minimal unit test? might be fast to add a deterministic check to CI that compares FP8 path against FP16 for a few seeds and shapes.
sam: I started one in my local branch. failing case attached to the repro script (seeded). commit: 7b3e2f4 (local).
benchmark-bot: quick numbers: FP8 path (matmul_fp8_pack_v2) = 2.1x throughput vs fp16 for seq=1536 batch=4, but correctness delta ~0.5 perplexity on eval set.
oncall: assigning fix owner — @kevin can you take a first pass? we should consider hotfix to force fp16 in prod until this is fixed.
kevin: will do. plan: (1) add strict scale-consistency assertion in matmul dispatcher when kv_cache is used, (2) add CI regression test that runs the repro shapes under seed, (3) if assertion trips in canary, fallback to fp16 and log metric.
anya: also check batching heuristics: we saw this only when batch contains mixed sequence lengths (padding path). maybe the packing reorders columns and loses per-column scale association.
sam: confirmed — mixed-length packing triggers different column layout. I think the pack kernel assumes homogeneous per-column scales.
jen: quick workaround env var: RW_FORCE_MATMUL_FP16=1. let's patch the dedicated fleets to set that flag for now.
oncall: created incident ticket INC-2026, setting priority P1 for dedicated fleets.
kevin: I'll open a branch and push tests + temp revert of pack_v2 selection to force fp16 for affected shapes. also will add telemetry for scale-deltas.
sam: thanks. attaching small diff idea for assertion guard:
```
# pseudo
if kv_cache_enabled and per_col_scale.std() > 0.005:
    raise ScaleInconsistencyError("per-column scale variance too high with KV cache")
```
anya: we should avoid hard crash in prod; prefer fallback + metric + trace id. but assert in CI is good.
kevin: agreed. will implement fallback + metric, and CI assert.
benchmark-bot: adding perf impact note: expected throughput drop ~1.9x when forcing fp16 for these shapes. still acceptable for correctness.
sam: thanks all. I'll collect reproducer logs and put them in the ticket. tagging @jen for rollout coordination. :thumbsup:
jen: on it — will coordinate hotfix rollout and update runbook.
kevin: I'll post PR link once ready and ping this thread.
sam: assigning follow-ups: kevin (fix + tests + fallback), jen (hotfix rollout), anya (CI test review), sam (repro artifacts + logs).
oncall: noted. leaving channel for alerts.
